quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near a blind pedestrian. It can be dangerous. Instead, yield to the pedestrian and drive safely when it is clear.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Work zones can be moving or stationary.
Work zones are marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay attention in work zones.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zones can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be fixed in one place or moving (like vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow). Work zones have orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: At night, how do you reduce the glare from oncoming headlights?

options.text: Look straight ahead.
Look over your shoulder.
Look at the center of the road.
Look to the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming drivers do not dim their lights, watch the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights, as the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must let traffic in the lanes you want to enter go first. Be ready to stop if needed. You can keep going if there is no other traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Traffic violations in work zones have the same fines as normal driving violations.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Only slow down if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to stop for equipment. Driving safely through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On vertical traffic signals, red is always on top and green is always on the bottom. On horizontal signals, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, park completely off the main road if you can.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones on highways. These diamond-shaped signs have black lettering or symbols and warn that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means parking is not allowed.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Slower drivers must stay in the right lane. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on interstate highways. If you miss your exit, you must go to the next one.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug, whether it is illegal, prescribed, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as a yield sign.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing crossbuck sign is a yield sign. You must yield the right-of-way to any trains and railroad equipment.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are especially slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Give yourself extra space to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially right after rain starts. Water on the road can cause hydroplaning, where your wheels lose grip. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush. Give yourself extra stopping distance.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and reduce visibility.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. Driving too slowly can also be dangerous because other drivers may make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: The broken yellow line side allows passing. The solid yellow line side does not allow passing.

questions.question: When parallel parking, park within ____ of the curb.

options.text: 10 inches
12 inches
18 inches
24 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches
questions.explanation: When parallel parking, your wheels should be parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb. Park only where it will not block traffic and where other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use high beam headlights to see better.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams in fog. Use low beams or fog lights instead.

questions.question: Can you text while driving?

options.text: Yes, if you can text without looking at your phone.
No, never.
Yes, if you use voice-to-text.
Yes, if you only look away for a moment.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is illegal in Rhode Island. Using your phone while driving distracts you from the road.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who arrived first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: Drivers should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If multiple drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: Why should you be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians. They are smaller and harder to spot than cars. Always watch for them.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid line and a broken line, you can pass from the side with the broken line if it is safe.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It causes hearing loss.
It causes pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It causes poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak can let these gases, including carbon monoxide, enter the passenger area. Fix leaks right away.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: When driving in thick fog, slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn on your high beam lights.
Turn on your low beam lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam lights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam lights in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off the moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Fog lights can help too.
